gml:Dictionary.gml:description: This dictionary defines quantities produced or consumed by a rigid inclusion design that are carried as parameters rather than as fixed schema elements. Two kinds of entry are present. The first are the method-specific arching coefficients, which exist only inside one named arching model and are carried in the coefficient property of a diggs:ArchingCoefficients object; each is conditioned on the arching model that defines it, so a file reporting a Hewlett-Randolph efficiency under a Zaeske design does not validate. The second are design quantities that are common to several practices or vary too freely to justify a fixed schema element - the geometry and stiffness ratios that gate whether an arching method's unit-cell idealisation applies to a given layout, open-ended since a future method may add its own - carried in diggs:DesignRITreatedAreaType/methodApplicabilityRatio. The active earth pressure coefficient, once considered for this dictionary, turned out not to need it: a single, always-the-same-formula quantity, now the typed element diggs:DesignRILTPType/activeEarthPressureCoefficient instead. Quantities that every arching practice ultimately produces - the stress delivered to the column head and the stress reaching the soil between heads - are deliberately NOT here: they are typed elements on diggs:DesignRILTPType, because they are the two values on which designs prepared under different standards can actually be compared.
gml:Dictionary.gml:name: DIGGS Rigid Inclusion Design Properties

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The Marston arching coefficient Cc,arch used in the BS 8006-1 arching formulation to express the proportion of embankment load transferred onto the inclusion caps. Defined only within the Marston/BS arching model; it has no meaning under a dome-arching or load-displacement-compatibility formulation, which is why this entry is conditioned on the arching model rather than offered unconditionally.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Marston arching coefficient

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The ratio p'c/sigma'v of the vertical stress carried on the inclusion cap to the average vertical stress at the base of the embankment, as computed by the BS 8006-1 arching formulation. A ratio of two pressures rather than a bare dimensionless number: stating the quantity class forces both quantities to be pressures and prevents the value being read as a load fraction, which is a different quantity (see arching_efficiency_cap).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Cap stress ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The arching efficiency Ecrown evaluated at the crown of the soil dome in the Hewlett-Randolph model - the proportion of embankment weight carried by the inclusions when the crown of the arch governs. Hewlett-Randolph evaluates efficiency at two locations and adopts the lesser; this is one of the two. See arching_efficiency_minimum for the adopted value.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Crown arching efficiency
diggs:Definition.diggs:authority: Hewlett, W.J. and Randolph, M.F. (1988), Ground Engineering 21(3)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The arching efficiency Ecap evaluated at the inclusion cap in the Hewlett-Randolph model - the proportion of embankment weight carried by the inclusions when the cap governs. The second of the two locations at which Hewlett-Randolph evaluates efficiency.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Cap arching efficiency
diggs:Definition.diggs:authority: Hewlett, W.J. and Randolph, M.F. (1988), Ground Engineering 21(3)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The governing arching efficiency Emin adopted by the Hewlett-Randolph model, being the lesser of the crown and cap efficiencies. This is the value the design carries forward; the two component efficiencies are reported alongside it so that a reviewer can see which location governed.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Minimum arching efficiency
diggs:Definition.diggs:authority: Hewlett, W.J. and Randolph, M.F. (1988), Ground Engineering 21(3)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The passive earth pressure coefficient Kp = (1 + sin phi'p) / (1 - sin phi'p) of the platform or embankment fill, as used in the Hewlett-Randolph dome-arching solution. Note that this is a PEAK friction angle quantity in that formulation, whereas the friction angle adopted for arching is often a critical-state value; the two are not interchangeable and the design should state which was used.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Passive earth pressure coefficient
diggs:Definition.diggs:authority: Hewlett, W.J. and Randolph, M.F. (1988), Ground Engineering 21(3)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The critical stress ratio Kcrit = tan^2(45 deg + phi'/2) governing the vertical stress distribution in the Zaeske multi-shell arching model adopted by EBGEO. Numerically this is the Rankine passive coefficient, but it is a distinct entry from passive_earth_pressure_coefficient because it enters a different formulation and is conditioned on a different arching model; merging them would let a file report an EBGEO quantity under a Hewlett-Randolph design and validate.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Critical stress ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The lateral earth pressure coefficient K used in the adapted-Terzaghi formulation of the load-displacement-compatibility method. A RECOMMENDED CONSTANT RATHER THAN A PROJECT-SPECIFIC QUANTITY: the method carries a recommended value of 0.75, which is one of the reasons it is a dictionary entry - the recommendation and its provenance can be recorded here in a way a schema element could not. State the value actually adopted; a design departing from 0.75 should say so.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Adapted-Terzaghi lateral earth pressure coefficient
diggs:Definition.diggs:authority: FHWA GEC-13 (Ground Modification Methods Reference Manual)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The Prandtl bearing capacity factor Nq applied at the inclusion head in the ASIRI punching check, evaluated at the critical-state friction angle of the platform fill. Governs the stress that can be delivered to the head before the fill punches around it.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Head punching bearing factor

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The geometric ratio h/(s-d) of platform or embankment height above the inclusion heads to the clear spacing between inclusions. One of the geometric limits that determine whether a given arching method is applicable to a given layout; a method used outside the ratio range it was validated over is not defensible, which is what makes this worth stating rather than leaving to be recomputed.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Arching height ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The geometric ratio d/s of inclusion diameter to centre-to-centre spacing. A second method-applicability limit, and the quantity most directly related to the area replacement ratio; carry both rather than either alone, since practices state their limits against different ones of the two.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Diameter to spacing ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The ratio sx/sy of the two orthogonal centre-to-centre spacings of a rectangular grid. Unity for a square grid. Methods derived for square or triangular layouts carry limits on how far from unity this may go before the unit-cell idealisation stops holding.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Spacing aspect ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The ratio ks,T/ks of the stiffness of the improved composite ground to that of the untreated ground, used by EBGEO as a gate on whether its method may be applied. THE GATE VALUE IS NOT STATED HERE. The threshold this ratio must exceed is a pass/fail requirement on method validity, not a design value, and belongs in a diggs:DesignConformanceCriterion that names this property. That keeps the requirement where a reviewer looks for requirements and lets it differ by project or edition. The commonly cited threshold has not been verified against a retrievable clause; the criterion carrying it should cite its own source.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Subgrade stiffness ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The ratio of the vertical stress carried by the soft soil between inclusion heads to the vertical stress that would act there without arching. FHWA GEC-13 Eq 3-23.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Stress reduction ratio (SRR)
